reuse.why: Most actions share getEditableCategories and existing budget primitives, but copyPreviousMonth independently implements the shared eligibility policy.

duplication.why: Category queries are consolidated, but the hidden-category and saved-template predicates remain duplicated between SQL and JavaScript.

placement.why: Selection policy and budget operations remain in the budget actions module, with handler registration using the established application layer.

scope.why: Changes are confined to the requested month-wide actions, their handler registration, and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: The shared selection helper improves ownership, but maintaining parallel eligibility implementations for copying and other actions invites policy drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: copyPreviousMonth bypasses getEditableCategories and applies hidden, template, and fixed-group exclusions locally.

disguised_duplication.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: getEditableCategoryFilter expresses hidden and saved-template exclusions in SQL, while copyPreviousMonth and hasSavedTemplates reshape those decisions into JavaScript.

abstraction_drift.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/actions.ts: the shared selection helpers gain includeHidden and its conditional SQL branch, while copyPreviousMonth independently maintains the evolving eligibility policy.
